s: Which organisation was scheduled to be hosted by France in 2026?

s: Where is COP31 to be held?
x: COP31 is at Antalya, Türkiye; COP30 was at Belém, Brazil, and Bonn hosts the UNFCCC HQ.

s: Which country chairs ASEAN in 2026?
x: The Philippines chairs ASEAN in 2026; Kyrgyzstan chairs the SCO.

s: Who is the Special Guest at the 18th BRICS Summit hosted by India in 2026?
x: Bangladesh PM Tariq Rahman is the Special Guest under Neighbourhood First; BRICS has 11 members.

s: On which dates was the 18th BRICS Summit held in New Delhi?
x: The 18th BRICS Summit was held at Bharat Mandapam on 12-13 September 2026, not 17-19 September.

s: In which year was the New Development Bank, headquartered in Shanghai, established?
x: The NDB was established in 2015, not 2009 (the year of the first BRICS summit).

s: What was the outcome of the 16th BRICS NSA meeting chaired by Ajit Doval in June 2026?
o: A BRICS counter-terrorism convention was signed
Bangladesh was admitted as a BRICS member
The NSAs could not agree a joint statement on terrorism
A BRICS joint military exercise was announced
x: At the 16th BRICS NSA meeting in New Delhi the NSAs could not agree a joint statement on terrorism.

s: Who is the President of the New Development Bank (NDB), headquartered in Shanghai?
x: The NDB, headquartered in Shanghai, is headed by President Dilma Rousseff.

s: Where was the 16th BRICS Trade Ministers' Meeting, which concluded on 7 August 2026, held?
x: It was held at Sawai Man Mahal, Jaipur. Bhopal hosted the BRICS Culture Ministers' Meeting and Goa the Ocean and Polar S&T Working Group meeting.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about meetings held during India's BRICS Presidency in 2026?
o: The Heads of National Statistical Offices met in Lucknow on 3–4 August
The Environment Ministers' Meeting at Bharat Mandapam adopted the Jaipur Declaration
The statistics meeting's theme was "Quality Statistics as Driver of Change"
The BRICS ICT Track meeting was held in Pune on 17–21 August
x: The Environment Ministers' Meeting adopted a Joint Statement, not the Jaipur Declaration.

s: Where was the BRICS Disaster Risk Reduction Ministers' meeting of July 2026 held?
x: It was held in New Delhi, led by the NDMA and MHA. Chandigarh, Nagpur and Hyderabad were linked with other BRICS ministerial meetings.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with a BRICS ministerial meeting held during India's 2026 Presidency?
o: Ocean and Polar S&T Working Group — Chennai
x: The Ocean and Polar S&T Working Group meeting was held in Goa, not Chennai. The Trade, Tourism and Culture meetings were associated respectively with the Jaipur Consensus, Jaipur Declaration and Bhopal Declaration.

s: Where was the 2026 meeting of Heads of BRICS Anti-Drug Agencies held?
x: The Heads of BRICS Anti-Drug Agencies met in Guwahati; the Women Ministers met in Kochi.

s: What is the theme of the 18th BRICS Summit hosted by India in 2026?
o: AI for Sustainable Development and Global South cooperation
Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability
Building for Resilience, Inclusion, Cooperation and Security
Bridging Regions for Inclusive Cooperation and Sustainability
x: The theme spells out BRICS as 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability'. 'AI for Sustainable Development and Global South cooperation' was linked with the Science Academies Forum.

s: Where was the 5th BRICS Geospatial Working Group meeting held in July 2026?
x: The 5th BRICS Geospatial Working Group meeting was held at IIT Tirupati, Yerpedu, from July 20 to 22. IIT Hyderabad hosted the Science Academies Forum, while Kochi hosted the BRICS Women Ministers’ meeting.

s: Which of the following pairs related to India's polar research is correctly matched?
x: Maitri was established in 1989. Dakshin Gangotri dates to 1983–84 (later closed), Bharati to 2012, and NCPOR was set up in 1998 at Vasco da Gama, Goa.

s: Where was the first in-person technical meeting of the BRICS DRR Working Group (June 2026) held?
x: The DRR Working Group met in person at Puri; the 3rd DRR Ministers' meeting was in New Delhi.

s: Which declaration was adopted at the 11th BRICS Culture Ministers' meeting (2026)?
x: The Culture Ministers met at Bhopal and adopted the Bhopal Declaration; Jaipur gave the Tourism Ministers' declaration.

s: Where was the BRICS Heads of National Statistical Offices meeting on 'Quality Statistics as Driver of Change' held?
x: The Heads of NSOs met in Lucknow on 3-4 August 2026 (MoSPI).

s: Where was the BRICS Youth and Sports Ministers' meeting (August 2026) held?
x: The Youth and Sports Ministers met in Visakhapatnam on 22-23 August 2026, chaired by Mansukh Mandaviya.

s: Which of the following BRICS 2026 ministerial meetings is INCORRECTLY matched with its venue?
x: The 16th BRICS Health Ministers met in Chandigarh; Jaipur hosted the Trade, Tourism and Industry Ministers.

s: Which city hosted the 12th BRICS Labour and Employment Ministers' Meeting in July 2026?
x: The 12th BRICS Labour and Employment Ministers met in Hyderabad on 15-16 July 2026; Nagpur hosted Transport and Kochi Women Ministers.

s: Which declaration was adopted at the 2026 meeting of Heads of BRICS Anti-Drug Agencies?
x: The Heads of Anti-Drug Agencies met at Guwahati on 6-7 July 2026 and adopted the Guwahati Declaration.

s: Where was the 16th BRICS Health Ministers' Meeting of 2026, which launched the BRICS Mission for Healthy Lifestyle, held?
x: The 16th BRICS Health Ministers' Meeting was held at Chandigarh and launched the BRICS Mission for Healthy Lifestyle.

s: Where was the 13th BRICS Education Ministers' Meeting held on 5-7 August 2026?
x: The 13th BRICS Education Ministers' Meeting was held at Bhubaneswar on 5-7 August 2026.

s: Which programme was launched at the 12th BRICS Labour and Employment Ministers' Meeting at Hyderabad (July 2026)?
x: The 12th BRICS Labour and Employment Ministers' Meeting at Hyderabad (15-16 Jul 2026) adopted a ministerial declaration and the BRICS CONNECT programme.

s: Which consensus document was adopted at the 16th BRICS Trade Ministers' Meeting chaired by Piyush Goyal in August 2026?
x: The 16th BRICS Trade Ministers' Meeting at Sawai Man Mahal, Jaipur, adopted the Jaipur Consensus.

s: The joint statement of the 3rd BRICS Disaster Risk Reduction Ministers' Meeting (New Delhi, July 2026) builds on the Udaipur Declaration (2016) and which other declaration?
x: The 2026 BRICS DRR joint statement builds on the Udaipur Declaration (2016) and the Kazan Declaration (2024).

s: Where is the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR) located?
x: NCPOR (1998) is at Vasco da Gama, Goa; it hosted the 8th BRICS Ocean and Polar S&T Working Group in 2026.

s: Where was the 3rd BRICS Transport Ministers' Meeting, chaired by Nitin Gadkari, held in July 2026?
x: The 3rd BRICS Transport Ministers met at Nagpur on 11-12 July 2026.

s: Which city hosted the 2nd BRICS Anti-Corruption Working Group meeting in August 2026?
x: DoPT hosted the 2nd BRICS Anti-Corruption Working Group at Hyderabad on 4-5 August 2026.

s: Where was the BRICS Women Ministers' Meeting held in July 2026?
x: BRICS Women Ministers met at Kochi on 8-9 July 2026.

s: In which year was India's Antarctic research station Bharati set up?
x: Bharati dates from 2012; Maitri from 1989 and Dakshin Gangotri from 1983-84.

s: At the 52nd G7 Summit Outreach Session, disruption in which region was discussed as a concern affecting LPG, LNG, diesel and fertilisers?
x: The concern related to disruption in the Strait of Hormuz, with possible effects on LPG, LNG, diesel and fertilisers. The other straits were not identified in this context.

s: Where was the 52nd G7 Summit Outreach Session (June 2026) held?
x: The 52nd G7 Summit was held at Évian-les-Bains, France, not Paris, at the invitation of President Macron.

s: In what capacity does the European Union participate in the G7?
x: The G7 is informal, with no treaty and no permanent secretariat; the EU participates as a non-enumerated member.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's proposals at the 52nd G7 Summit Outreach Session?
o: IMPACT stands for International Mobilisation Partnership for Accelerating Connectivity and Trade
India proposed a Global Skills Partnership
IMPACT envisages G7 capital, India's talent and Global South ownership
IMPACT envisages India's capital, G7 talent and Global North ownership
x: IMPACT pairs G7 capital with India's talent under Global South ownership, not the reverse.

s: For which time was India invited to the G7 at the 52nd G7 Summit?
x: India was invited for the 13th time, and for the 7th consecutive year.

s: For what did the 52nd G7 Summit adopt a declaration on securing supply chains?
x: The G7 adopted a Declaration on Securing Supply Chains for Critical Minerals through PGII.

s: What did India and the EU announce during the G7 Summit (June 2026)?
x: India-EU FTA negotiations were concluded, with signing due by the end of 2026.

s: What does IMPACT, India's proposal at the 52nd G7 Summit, stand for?
o: International Mobilisation Partnership for Accelerating Connectivity and Trade
India-Mediterranean Partnership for Agriculture, Climate and Technology
International Mission for Poverty Alleviation and Climate Transition
Indo-Pacific Maritime Partnership for Assured Connectivity and Trade
x: IMPACT = International Mobilisation Partnership for Accelerating Connectivity and Trade, combining G7 capital, India's talent and Global South ownership.

s: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the G20?
x: Argentina, Mexico, South Africa and Turkey are G20 members; Nigeria is not.

s: What was the theme of the outreach of the 52nd G7 Summit at Évian-les-Bains (June 2026)?
o: Working Together to Address Major International Challenges
Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability

s:
Consider the following statements about the G7:

x: The G7 is informal, with no treaty and no permanent secretariat; the EU participates as a non-enumerated member.

s: The Safran–SatSure MoU signed during the France–India Year of Innovation concerns which area?
x: The Safran–SatSure MoU concerns AI geospatial intelligence. Maritime, financial and health intelligence are not the areas associated with this MoU.

s: The India–France Innovation Roadmap 2030 is based on which combination?
x: Its stated basis is Viksit Bharat 2047 together with France 2030; Horizon 2047 is part of its wider background.

s: The India–France Innovation Roadmap 2030 builds on which combination?
o: Horizon 2047 roadmap and India–France Year of Innovation 2026
India–France Declaration on AI 2025 and AI Impact Summit 2026
Horizon 2047 roadmap and AI Action Summit 2025
India–France Year of Innovation 2026 and AI Impact Summit 2026
x: The Roadmap builds on the Horizon 2047 roadmap and the India–France Year of Innovation 2026.

s: On which date were India–France ties elevated to a Special Global Strategic Partnership?
x: India–France ties were elevated to a Special Global Strategic Partnership on 17 February 2026.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the India–France Innovation Roadmap 2030 is incorrect?
o: The aeronautics campus is proposed at Paris with the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.
The Trusted AI pillar draws on the India–France Declaration on AI 2025, the AI Action Summit in France 2025 and the AI Impact Summit in India 2026.
ICMR is associated with France’s Health Data Hub for health-data cooperation.
x: The incorrect statement places the aeronautics campus at Paris. The campus is associated with Kanpur and the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship; the other statements correctly describe the roadmap’s pillars.

s: The India-France ATL Bridge, launched at India Innovates 2026 in Nice, is a collaboration between the Atal Innovation Mission (NITI Aayog) and which body?
x: The ATL Bridge was launched by the Atal Innovation Mission of NITI Aayog and the Dassault Systèmes Foundation.

s: Which country hosted the AI Impact Summit in 2026?
x: India hosted the AI Impact Summit in 2026; France had hosted the AI Action Summit in 2025.

s: At which conference was the International Solar Alliance launched?
x: ISA was launched at COP21 in 2015; not all UN members are its members.

s: Which country hosted the AI Action Summit in 2025?
x: The AI Action Summit was held in France in 2025; India hosted the AI Impact Summit in 2026.

s:
Consider the following statements about the International Solar Alliance:
1. It was launched at COP21 in Paris in 2015.
2. All members of the United Nations are its members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The ISA was launched by India and France at COP21 (2015); not all UN members have joined it.

s: Which was the first country to sign a Mutual Recognition of Qualifications agreement with India (2018)?
x: France was the first country to have a Mutual Recognition of Qualifications agreement with India, in 2018.

s: In which year did India and France establish their Strategic Partnership?
x: India and France have been strategic partners since 1998; ties were raised to a Special Global Strategic Partnership on 17 February 2026.

s: What is the full form of CEFIPRA, an India-France institution?
o: Centre for Indo-French Promotion of Applied Research
Indo-French Centre for Promotion of Advanced Research
Council of Engineering for France-India Programme of Research and Applications
Indo-French Centre for Industrial Partnership and Research
x: CEFIPRA is the Indo-French Centre for Promotion of Advanced Research.

s: What is Australia's contribution under the ACITI partnership?
x: ACITI links Canada's AI research, India's digital scale and Australia's critical minerals.

s: President Droupadi Murmu’s visit to which country on July 20, 2026 was the first-ever visit by an Indian President to that country?
x: Moldova received the first-ever visit by an Indian President on July 20, 2026. North Macedonia and Romania were also included in the visit, but the first-ever presidential visit specifically concerned Moldova.

s: President Droupadi Murmu's July 2026 visit to North Macedonia was the first since ties began in which year?
x: India–North Macedonia ties began in 1995, and the July 21–22, 2026 visit was the first such visit since.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about President Murmu's visit to Romania (23 July 2026)?
o: Three agreements were signed in Science and Technology, Sports, and Indian Studies
2026 was designated the India–Romania Year of Innovation
An ICCR Indian Studies Chair was set up at the University of Bucharest
ITEC slots were doubled with AI and cyber diplomacy courses
x: It was 2028, not 2026, that was named the India–Romania Year of Innovation.

s: What did the India–Australia Partnership for Accelerated Cooperation and Transformation (PACTS) replace?
o: The Australia–Canada–India Technology and Innovation Partnership
The India–Australia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership of 2020
The 2020 Framework Arrangement on Cyber and Cyber-Enabled Critical Technology Cooperation
x: PACTS replaced the 2020 Framework Arrangement on Cyber and Cyber-Enabled Critical Technology Cooperation. The other options are separate agreements or partnerships and were not replaced by PACTS.

s: Who oversees PACTS with Australia on India's side?
x: PACTS is overseen by India's Deputy NSA, with Australia's Deputy Secretary, International and Security Group.

s: What did the '3Ts' focus stand for during President Murmu's Moldova visit (July 2026)?
x: The visit focused on the 3Ts – Trade, Technology and Talent – and ITEC slots for Moldova were doubled.

s: In which year was the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR) established?
x: ICCR was set up in 1950; 1964 is when the ITEC programme of the MEA began.

s: In which year was the India–Australia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership established?
x: The India–Australia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership dates from 2020. The other years do not match the reported year of establishment.

s: ACITI is a technology and innovation partnership of India, Australia and which other country?
x: ACITI = Australia-Canada-India Technology and Innovation Partnership, launched 9 July 2026; it includes Canada, not Japan.

s: Which ministry manages the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) programme started in 1964?
x: ITEC was started in 1964 and is managed by the Ministry of External Affairs.

s: What is the capital of Moldova, which President Droupadi Murmu visited in July 2026?
x: Chisinau is the capital of Moldova; Murmu's visit on 20 July 2026 was the first by an Indian President.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI)?
x: CDRI (2019) is based in New Delhi; the ISA is at Gurugram.

s: What is the capital of North Macedonia, which President Murmu visited in July 2026?
x: Skopje is the capital of North Macedonia; its currency is the Denar.

s: Australia's agreement to export uranium to India for civil nuclear energy builds on which agreement?
x: Australia's uranium exports for India's civil nuclear plants build on the 2014 Civil Nuclear Cooperation Agreement.

s: Whose initiative is the Critical Minerals Global Supply Chain Observatory launched in New Delhi on 5 June 2026?
o: TEXMiN, IIT Kharagpur and University of Oxford
IIT Bombay, NITI Aayog and University of Cambridge
Ministry of Mines, IIT (ISM) Dhanbad and Imperial College London
TEXMiN, IIT (ISM) Dhanbad and University of Cambridge
x: The Observatory was launched by TEXMiN, IIT (ISM) Dhanbad and the University of Cambridge.

s: The 25th India-China Special Representatives talks, held in Beijing on 25 August 2026, were between Ajit Doval and whom?
x: The Special Representatives talks were between Ajit Doval and Wang Yi; Doval met Vice President Han Zheng separately.

s: In which year was the India-China Special Representatives mechanism established?
x: The SR mechanism dates from 2003; its 25th meeting was in Beijing on 25 August 2026.

s: In which year was India's National Critical Mineral Mission launched?
x: The National Critical Mineral Mission dates from 2025.

s: Which group of countries was elected as non-permanent members of the UN Security Council for the term 2027–2028 at the 80th UNGA session?
o: India, Portugal, Austria, Panama and Somalia
Denmark, Greece, Pakistan, Panama and Somalia
Argentina, Germany, Netherlands, Chile and Costa Rica
Portugal, Kyrgyzstan, Trinidad and Tobago, Zimbabwe and Austria
x: Portugal, Kyrgyzstan, Trinidad and Tobago, Zimbabwe and Austria were elected as non-permanent members for 2027–2028. Denmark, Greece, Pakistan, Panama and Somalia were the members being replaced because their terms ended on 31 December 2026.

s: At which event did António Guterres launch the Global Call to Action on Methane in June 2026?
x: The Global Call to Action on Methane was launched at London Climate Action Week 2026.

s: Which two WEOG countries were elected to the UN Security Council for 2027-28, both for the 4th time?
x: Portugal (134 votes) and Austria (131) won the WEOG seats; Denmark and Greece are among the outgoing members.

s: At which conference was the Global Methane Pledge launched?
x: The Global Methane Pledge (cut 30% from 2020 levels by 2030) was launched at COP26, Glasgow, not COP28.

s: At the Bonn Climate Conference (SB64), developed countries were urged to triple adaptation finance to what by 2035?
x: The call was to triple adaptation finance from USD 40 bn to USD 120 bn by 2035.

s: By which year does the UN Political Declaration on HIV/AIDS (June 2026) aim to end AIDS?
x: The declaration (149 for, 8 against, 14 abstained) aims to end AIDS by 2030 (SDG-3).

s: Which of the following countries is NOT among those elected to the UN Security Council for 2027-28?
x: Pakistan is an outgoing member whose term ends on 31 December 2026; the elected five are Portugal, Kyrgyzstan, Trinidad and Tobago, Zimbabwe and Austria.

s: Where was COP30 of the UNFCCC held?
x: COP30 was held at Belém, Brazil; COP31 is at Antalya, Türkiye.

s: Where is the headquarters of the UNFCCC, which held the SB64 session in June 2026?
x: The UNFCCC (1992) is headquartered in Bonn, Germany, where the 64th Subsidiary Bodies session was held on 8-18 June 2026.

s: Where is the headquarters of UNAIDS located?
x: UNAIDS was set up in 1994 and is headquartered at Geneva.

s: By how much does the Global Methane Pledge aim to cut methane emissions by 2030?
x: The Global Methane Pledge (COP26 Glasgow, 2021) aims to cut methane by 30% from 2020 levels by 2030.

s: How many members does the UN Security Council have?
x: The UNSC has 15 members: 5 permanent and 10 non-permanent members elected for two years.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about international initiatives in June 2026?
o: Argentina was among the countries that also joined the Pax Silicon initiative with India
The Mombasa Declaration was adopted at the 10th Our Ocean Conference
The Mombasa Declaration involved 15 countries opposing IUU fishing
Bolivia declared a 90-day state of emergency
x: The Mombasa Declaration was made at the 11th Our Ocean Conference, not the 10th.

s: At which event did India join Pax Silicon, a US-led initiative on trusted supply chains?
x: India joined Pax Silicon at the AI Impact Summit in February 2026, then signed the Joint Declaration on AI Opportunities at the 2nd Pax Silicon Summit.

s: What is the Mombasa Declaration, signed by 15 countries at the 11th Our Ocean Conference, against?
x: The Mombasa Declaration targets illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing.

s: For what purpose does AUKUS plan underwater drones by 2027?
x: AUKUS (2021) announced underwater drones for subsea cable security by 2027.

s: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the Five Eyes intelligence alliance?
x: Five Eyes comprises the US, UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand; Japan is not a member.

s: Which countries are members of AUKUS, formed in 2021?
o: Australia, UK and United Arab Emirates
x: AUKUS (2021) is a security pact of Australia, the United Kingdom and the United States.

s: How many countries, including India, signed the Joint Declaration on AI Opportunities at the 2nd Pax Silicon Summit in Washington, D.C. (June 2026)?
x: India and 34 other countries (35 in all) signed the Joint Declaration on AI Opportunities at the 2nd Pax Silicon Summit.

s: "Naoero" is the indigenous name of which Pacific country?
x: Naoero is Nauru's indigenous name; it has no official capital, Yaren being its administrative centre.

s: Which programme did Nauru launch as a non-debt climate-finance mechanism?
o: Nauru Economic and Climate Resilience Citizenship Program
x: Nauru launched the Nauru Economic and Climate Resilience Citizenship Program as a non-debt climate-finance mechanism.

s: Nauru (Naoero) has no official capital; which is its administrative centre?
x: Nauru has no official capital; Yaren is only the administrative centre.

s:
Consider the following statements about Nauru (Naoero):
1. It is the third-smallest country by area.
2. Its currency is the Australian Dollar.
3. Its country code was changed after the renaming.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The country code NRO remains unchanged.

s: Who is the President of Nauru who announced the country's new name 'Republic of Naoero' in July 2026?
x: Nauru's President David Adeang announced the renaming to Republic of Naoero on 31 July 2026.

s: The G20 Common Framework, developed with the Paris Club, addresses the debt of which group of countries?
x: The G20 Common Framework, with the Paris Club, is intended for the debt of Low Income Countries. The other categories do not describe its stated target group.

s: Which country is scheduled to host the BRICS grouping in 2026?
x: India is scheduled to host BRICS in 2026. Kyrgyzstan, the Philippines and the United States are associated with the SCO, ASEAN and G20 respectively, not BRICS.

s: Which country is hosting APEC in 2026?
x: China is hosting APEC in 2026, while Turkey is hosting NATO.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the 52nd G7 Summit is incorrect?
o: It is scheduled for 15–17 June 2026 at Évian-les-Bains in Haute-Savoie, France.
Macron invited Modi during his visit to Mumbai on 17 February 2026.
The 52nd G7 Summit is scheduled to be hosted by the United States.
The first G6 summit was held at Rambouillet in 1975, and Canada joined in 1976.
x: The incorrect statement is that the 52nd G7 Summit is to be hosted by the United States; France is the host in 2026. The summit is scheduled at Évian-les-Bains from 15–17 June 2026, while the historical details about Rambouillet and Canada are correct.

s: Which grouping is correctly matched with its 2026 host country?
x: France hosts the G7 in 2026; Kyrgyzstan hosts the SCO, the Philippines ASEAN and the United States the G20.

s: Where was the 36th NATO summit, held on 7-8 July 2026, hosted?
x: The 36th NATO summit was held at Ankara, Türkiye, and adopted the Ankara Summit Declaration.

s: Where is the 2026 G20 summit under the US presidency to be held?
x: The G20 summit is to be held at Trump National Doral, Miami, on 14–15 December 2026.

s: Where was the first G6 summit held in 1975?
x: The first G6 summit was at Rambouillet in 1975; Canada joined in 1976.

s: In which year was Russia suspended from the G8?
x: Russia was admitted in 1998 (G8) and suspended in 2014 after Crimea.

s: What level of defence spending does the Hague commitment endorsed at NATO's 2026 summit set?
x: The Hague commitment (2025) sets 5% of GDP by 2035, of which 3.5% is core defence.

s: Which country hosts the 53rd G7 summit in 2027?
x: The 52nd G7 is in Évian, France (2026); the US hosts the 53rd in 2027.

s: Which country is the ASEAN chair in 2026?
x: The Philippines chairs ASEAN in 2026.

s: Which of the following grouping–2026 host pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Kyrgyzstan, not Kazakhstan, chairs the SCO in 2026, with the summit at Bishkek.

s: Where was the 51st G7 Summit held in June 2025?
x: The 51st G7 Summit was at Kananaskis, Canada (June 2025); the 52nd was at Évian-les-Bains, France (June 2026).

s: Which country joined the G6 in 1976, making it the G7?
x: The first G6 summit was at Rambouillet in 1975; Canada joined in 1976. Russia was admitted in 1998 and suspended in 2014.

s: Which document was adopted at the 36th NATO Summit held at Ankara in July 2026?
x: The 36th NATO Summit (Ankara, 7-8 July 2026) adopted the Ankara Summit Declaration and endorsed the 2025 Hague 5% commitment.

s: Where is the 2026 G20 Summit under the US Presidency scheduled to be held?
x: The 2026 G20 Summit is set for Trump National Doral, Miami, on 14-15 December 2026.

s: Where is the headquarters of the New Development Bank?
x: The New Development Bank, established in 2014, is headquartered in Shanghai.

s: Which one of the following is correct about the institutional structure of BRICS?
o: It has no permanent headquarters and follows a rotational presidency.
It has a permanent headquarters in Shanghai.
It has a permanent secretariat in New Delhi.
It has a permanent headquarters in Moscow.
x: BRICS has no permanent headquarters and follows a rotational presidency; Shanghai hosts the New Development Bank.

s: Which of the following is NOT included among the BRICS members?
x: Pakistan is not included in the listed BRICS membership. Indonesia, Ethiopia and Egypt are among the members listed alongside Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Iran.

s: Which Indian organisation is the nodal agency for India's participation in the BRICS Industrial Competence Centre?
x: The National Productivity Council is the nodal agency for India's participation in the BRICS Industrial Competence Centre, which supports manufacturing and MSMEs. UNIDO set up the Centre at its headquarters in Vienna, while the ILO and IMO are separate international organisations.

s: Who launched the website and logo of India's BRICS 2026 chairship?
x: EAM S. Jaishankar launched the website and the flower-petal logo in the colours of all members.

s: At whose headquarters is the BRICS Industrial Competence Centre set up?
x: The Centre was set up in 2024–25 at UNIDO HQ, Vienna, under the BRICS New Industrial Revolution Partnership.

s: What is the theme of India's BRICS Presidency 2026?
o: Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability
One Earth, One Family, One Future
x: India's BRICS 2026 theme is 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability'.

s: BRIC was established in 2009 by Brazil, Russia, India and which other country?
x: BRIC was founded in 2009 by Brazil, Russia, India and China; South Africa joined later.

s: Under the India–France Special Global Strategic Partnership outcomes, which initiative relates to the production of HAMMER missiles in India?
o: Joint Declaration on critical minerals supply chains
Indo-French Centre for AI in Health
x: The BEL–Safran joint venture is to produce HAMMER missiles in India. The Tata–Airbus initiative concerns helicopters, while the other options relate to AI and critical minerals.

s: What is TRISHNA, an ISRO-CNES satellite, meant for?
x: TRISHNA is associated with thermal infrared, not optical, imaging.

s: Regarding the India–France helicopter cooperation, which pair is correctly matched?
x: The H125 final assembly line is at Vemagal, Karnataka. The project is the Tata–Airbus H125, with first delivery in 2027.

s: Who co-chaired the 38th India–France Strategic Dialogue held in New Delhi on 13 January 2026 on behalf of India?
x: National Security Adviser Ajit Doval co-chaired the 38th India–France Strategic Dialogue for India. Emmanuel Bonne was the French co-chair, while S. Jaishankar and Hardeep Singh Puri are not identified as co-chairs of this dialogue.

s: The India–France Annual Foreign Ministers' Dialogue is aligned with which roadmap?
x: The dialogue is aligned with the Horizon 2047 Roadmap.

s: In February 2026, India and France upgraded their bilateral relationship to which status?
x: PM Modi and President Emmanuel Macron elevated India–France ties from Strategic Partnership to Special Global Strategic Partnership in February 2026. The other options do not describe the announced upgraded status.

s: With its proposed social-media restriction, France would become the second country to impose such a ban after which country?
x: France would be the second country after Australia, whose ban applies to those under 16.

s: Where is the Indo-French Centre for AI in Health to be set up?
x: The Indo-French Centre for AI in Health is at AIIMS New Delhi.

s: Since when have India and France had a strategic partnership?
x: The India–France strategic partnership dates to 1998; it became a Special Global Strategic Partnership in February 2026.

s: How many outcomes were announced when India–France ties became a Special Global Strategic Partnership?
x: Modi and Macron announced 21 outcomes in February 2026.

s: In the name of the US-led Pax Silica coalition, what do “Pax” and “Silica” signify respectively?
o: Supply chains and rare earth minerals
x: “Pax” means peace and “Silica” refers to a chip-making compound. The other options combine areas associated with the coalition rather than explaining its name.

s: When India joined Pax Silica, it became the first of which kind?
o: host of the inaugural Pax Silica Summit
x: India was invited later (not a founding member) and became the first major developing country and first non-US-ally strategic partner to join.

s: Which group comprised the inaugural observers of the Pax Silica coalition?
o: Canada, European Union, OECD and Taiwan
United States, Japan, South Korea and Australia
United Kingdom, Israel, Singapore and Qatar
x: The inaugural observers were Canada, the European Union, OECD and Taiwan. The other options either list core members or include countries not identified as inaugural observers.

s: When did India and Greece establish their Strategic Partnership?
x: The India–Greece Strategic Partnership dates to August 2023.

s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of core members of the Pax Silica coalition?
o: United States, Japan, South Korea and Australia
Canada, European Union, OECD and Taiwan
European Union, United Kingdom, OECD and Qatar
x: The United States, Japan, South Korea and Australia are all listed as core members of Pax Silica. Canada, the European Union, OECD and Taiwan are inaugural observers, making the other combinations incorrect.

s: Which alliance was formed by 15 global technology companies at the Munich Security Conference 2026?
x: The Trusted Tech Alliance was formed by 15 global technology companies at the Munich Security Conference 2026. Its aim is to establish joint verifiable standards covering transparency, security, governance and data protection.

s: Where was the India AI Impact Summit 2026 held?
x: The AI Impact Summit was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on 16–20 February 2026.

s: Where was the US-led Pax Silica launched in December 2025?
x: Pax Silica was launched at the inaugural Pax Silica Summit in Washington D.C. in December 2025; India joined in February 2026.

s:
Consider the following statements about India and Pax Silica:
1. India is a founding member of Pax Silica.
2. India joined on 20 February 2026 at the AI Impact Summit.
3. Pax Silica has 35 signatories.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: India is not a founding member; it joined on 20 February 2026, and the alliance has 35 signatories.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Pax Silica?
o: It aims to secure supply chains for critical minerals, semiconductors, AI infrastructure and logistics
It was launched in December 2025 at the inaugural summit in Washington D.C.
India signed to join it on 20 February 2026 during the AI Impact Summit
India was a founding member of Pax Silica
x: India was invited later and was not a founding member.

s: Which countries launched the Supply Chain Resilience Initiative in 2021?
x: The Supply Chain Resilience Initiative (2021) is a trilateral initiative of India, Japan and Australia.

s: In which city was the India-Canada energy statement of 27 January 2026 issued at India Energy Week?
x: The statement was issued at India Energy Week in Goa on 27 January 2026.

s: In which city was the India-Israel Joint Ministerial Statement of Intent on fisheries issued at the Global Summit on Blue Food Security 2026?
x: The statement was issued in Eilat, Israel, and covered RAS, biofloc, cage culture, aquaponics, mariculture and seaweed.

s: Since which year has Gaza been governed by Hamas?
x: Hamas has governed Gaza since 2007; Rafah shares a border with Egypt.

s: How much did the nine countries of the 'Peace Council' pledge for Gaza reconstruction?
x: The nine Peace Council countries pledged $70 billion; $10 billion was the US contribution.

s: Which of the following statements regarding Spain's proposed social media ban is incorrect?
o: Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez announced the plan.
The announcement was made at the World Government Summit in Dubai.
The plan includes strict age verification.
x: The incorrect statement is that the plan covers children under 18. Spain announced a proposed ban for children under 16, with strict age verification, at the World Government Summit in Dubai.

s: What was the theme of the 56th WEF Annual Meeting at Davos in January 2026?
x: The 56th WEF Annual Meeting (19–23 January 2026) had the theme 'A Spirit of Dialogue'.

s: What is India's status in the Board of Peace launched by Trump at Davos in January 2026?
x: India attends the 27-member Board of Peace only as an observer, without a vote.

s: How many members does the Board of Peace launched for Gaza reconstruction have?
x: The Board of Peace has 27 members; nine countries of the 'Peace Council' pledged $70 billion.

s: At which event did Spain's PM Pedro Sánchez announce a social media ban for children under 16?
x: Sánchez announced the plan at the World Government Summit, Dubai.

s: Which edition of the World Economic Forum Annual Meeting was held at Davos in January 2026?
x: The 56th WEF Annual Meeting was held at Davos on 19-23 January 2026, theme 'A Spirit of Dialogue'.

s: Rafah, where the first security forces for Gaza are to be deployed, borders which country?
x: Rafah, at the south of Gaza, borders Egypt.

s: In his Kuala Lumpur diaspora address, PM Modi called Tamil a gift from which country to the world?
x: Modi called Tamil a gift from India to the world, not from Malaysia; he said ties are guided by the 'IMPACT Partnership'.

s: NPCI International set up a payment linkage with which Malaysian entity?
x: NPCI International and PayNet Malaysia established a payment linkage.

s: In his Kuala Lumpur diaspora address, up to which generation of the Indian diaspora did PM Modi say OCI cards would be extended?
x: OCI cards were extended to the sixth generation of the Indian diaspora in Malaysia.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the outcomes of PM Modi's Malaysia visit?
o: The 10th India–Malaysia CEO Forum was held in Kuala Lumpur
AITIGA and MICECA were reviewed during the visit
The Thiruvalluvar Chair and Centre was set up at the University of Cyberjaya
Malaysia was recognised as a reliable supplier of palm oil
x: The Thiruvalluvar Chair and Centre was set up at Universiti Malaya; the University of Cyberjaya was linked to the CCRH MoU.

s: In which country was Nipah virus, mainly associated with Kerala in India, first identified in 1998?
x: Nipah was first identified in Malaysia in 1998; in India it is mainly found in Kerala.

s: What kind of joint India-Malaysia exercise is Harimau Shakti, held in December 2025?
x: Harimau Shakti is a joint Army exercise; Samudra Laksamana is the naval exercise.

s: Since when have India and Malaysia had a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership?
x: Diplomatic ties date to 1957; the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership dates to August 2024.

s: For which period do India and Malaysia co-chair the ADMM-Plus Counter-Terrorism Working Group?
x: India and Malaysia co-chair the ADMM-Plus Counter-Terrorism Working Group for 2024–2027.

s: What is Samudra Laksamana?
x: Samudra Laksamana is the India-Malaysia naval exercise; Harimau Shakti is the joint army exercise.

s: Which body was formalised during PM Modi's visit to Malaysia in February 2026 for cooperation in fintech, cybersecurity, AI and DPI?
x: The Malaysia-India Digital Council (MIDC) was formalised for fintech, cybersecurity, AI and digital public infrastructure.

s: At which university in Malaysia is a Thiruvalluvar Chair and Centre being set up?
x: A Thiruvalluvar Chair and Centre is to be set up at Universiti Malaya.

s: Who was the Prime Minister of Malaysia who hosted PM Modi on 7-8 February 2026?
x: PM Anwar Ibrahim hosted Modi; ties have been a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership since August 2024.

s: Who was the host Prime Minister of Malaysia during PM Modi's visit in February 2026?
x: PM Modi visited Malaysia on 7-8 February 2026; the host was PM Anwar Ibrahim.

s: Where did India and Greece sign a Joint Declaration of Intent on defence industrial cooperation?
x: Rajnath Singh and Nikolaos-Georgios Dendias signed it in New Delhi.

s: Who founded the Greco-Bactrian kingdom?
x: Diodotus founded the Greco-Bactrian kingdom; Demetrius later expanded into north-western India.

s: What defence-related arrangement was exchanged between India and Greece in 2026?
x: India and Greece exchanged the Bilateral Military Cooperation Plan 2026. The other options do not describe the defence arrangement exchanged between the two countries.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the India–Germany climate project under the International Climate Initiative?
o: It supports India's NDCs under the Paris Agreement
India is one of 12 priority countries of the initiative
It supports the goals of the CBD
Friedrich Merz is the German Chancellor associated with it
x: India is one of 14, not 12, priority countries of the IKI; the project supports NDCs and CBD goals under Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

s: Where is Greece's International Liaison Officer posted under India-Greece defence ties?
x: A Greek International Liaison Officer is posted at the IFC-IOR in Gurugram.

s: In which year was India's drug regulator CDSCO, which signed a pact with Brazil's ANVISA, established?
x: CDSCO was established in 1940 under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act; ANVISA dates to 1999.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL)?
o: It was set up after the turmeric and neem patent disputes
It is shared with patent offices under NDAs
Brazilian patent examiners can now use it
x: TKDL was established in 2001 by CSIR and AYUSH; 1942 is the year CSIR was established.

s: In which year was the Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL) established by CSIR and the Ministry of AYUSH?
x: The TKDL was set up in 2001, after the turmeric and neem patent disputes.

s: Which Greek port, majority-owned by China's COSCO, is seen as a gateway for IMEC?
x: Piraeus port, majority-owned by China's COSCO, is an IMEC gateway; Greece controls about 20% of global shipping tonnage.

s: In which city is Germany's International Climate Initiative (IKI), set up in 2008, based?
x: IKI was set up in 2008 and is based in Berlin; India is one of its 14 priority countries.

s: Who is the President of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)?
o: Union Minister of Science and Technology
x: CSIR, set up in 1942, has the Prime Minister as its President.

s: Who is the Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI)?
x: CDSCO, set up in 1940, is headed by DCGI Dr Rajeev Singh Raghuvanshi.

s: The Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI), launched by India in 2019, has how many pillars?
x: IPOI is a non-treaty, voluntary initiative with seven pillars, launched at the EAS in Bangkok in 2019.

s: What was India's solar module manufacturing capacity in late 2025?
x: India's module capacity was about 144 GW, while its cell capacity was only about 25 GW.

s: Which pair represents the platforms for India–Arab League cooperation?
o: International Climate Initiative and India–Arab League Dialogue
India–Arab League Dialogue and Arab–India Cooperation Forum
Arab–India Cooperation Forum and Traditional Knowledge Digital Library
India–Arab League Dialogue and International Climate Initiative
x: India–Arab League Dialogue and the Arab–India Cooperation Forum are the two platforms for India’s engagement with the Arab League. The International Climate Initiative and the Traditional Knowledge Digital Library are unrelated to this engagement.

s: In January 2026, the United States withdrew from how many international organisations, including the ISA?
x: The US withdrew from 66 international organisations, including the ISA, which it had joined in 2021.

s: At which conference did India and France launch the International Solar Alliance in 2015?
x: The ISA was launched at COP21 in Paris in 2015.

s: Which country presented its Accession Declaration to External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar for joining the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative?
x: Spain presented its Accession Declaration to S. Jaishankar for joining the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative. France, Germany and Poland are associated with the Weimar Triangle, not this accession.

s: In which year was the International Solar Alliance opened to all UN members by an amendment?
x: A 2020 amendment opened the ISA to all UN members, though it does not include all of them.

s: In which year did the United States join the International Solar Alliance?
x: The US joined the ISA late, in 2021, and withdrew in January 2026.

s: In which city was the Arab League founded on 22 March 1945?
x: The Arab League was founded in Cairo on 22 March 1945.

s:
Consider the following statements about the International Solar Alliance:
1. Its headquarters is at Gurugram.
2. It builds solar power plants in member countries.
3. It aims to mobilise $1 trillion of solar investment by 2030.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The ISA does not build plants; it facilitates finance, de-risking and capacity building. Statements 1 and 3 are correct.

s: At which summit did India launch the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI) in 2019?
x: India launched the IPOI, a non-treaty initiative with seven pillars, at the East Asia Summit in Bangkok in 2019.

s: Which of the following was NOT a founder member of the Arab League in 1945?
x: The Arab League was founded at Cairo on 22 March 1945 by Egypt, Iraq, Transjordan, Lebanon, Saudi Arabia and Syria; Yemen joined on 5 May 1945.

s: Who was the current President of South Korea in January 2026, while former President Yoon Suk Yeol was jailed for five years?
x: Lee Jae-myung was the current President of South Korea. Yoon Suk Yeol was the former President who was jailed for five years over the December 2024 martial law episode.

s: Shaya Mohsin Mohammed Al-Zindani, in the news in January 2026, is linked to which country?
x: Al-Zindani is linked to Yemen; Doumbouya is of Guinea, Touadéra of the Central African Republic and Museveni of Uganda.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India–Africa ties?
o: The African Union became a permanent G20 member in 2023 during India's Presidency
The African Continental Free Trade Area integrates a 54-country market
India accounts for about 21% of Africa's imports
India's trade with Africa is about $100 billion
x: India accounts for about 6% of Africa's imports; about 21% is China's share.

s: Under Kyrgyzstan's ban on Indian animal products, screening was arranged at Bishkek and which other airport?
x: Screening was arranged at Bishkek and Osh airports in Kyrgyzstan, not Tashkent.

s:
Assertion (A): India’s trade with Africa is about $100 billion, making India the 4th-largest partner.
Reason (R): China’s trade with Africa is over $200 billion.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both the assertion and the reason are true: India’s trade with Africa is about $100 billion and India is the 4th-largest partner, while China’s trade is over $200 billion. China’s trade figure does not explain India’s trade value or ranking, so the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.

s: Under whose presidency did the African Union become a permanent member of the G20 in 2023?
x: The AU became a permanent G20 member in 2023 during India's G20 Presidency.

s: Bharat Mandapam, venue of the AI Impact Summit 2026, also hosted which summit in 2023?
x: Bharat Mandapam hosted the 2023 G20 Summit under India's Presidency.

s: What is India's target for India-Africa trade?
x: The target is to double India–Africa trade, now about $100 billion, by 2030.

s: India accounts for about what share of Africa's imports?
x: India accounted for about 6% of Africa's imports.

s: Who won the presidency of Guinea, years after leading the 2021 coup that ousted Alpha Condé?
x: Mamady Doumbouya, who led the September 2021 coup, won Guinea's presidency with 86.7% of the vote.

s: Which leader began a seventh term as President of Uganda?
x: Yoweri Museveni of the National Resistance Movement began a seventh term as President of Uganda.

s: The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) integrates a market of how many countries?
x: AfCFTA integrates a 54-country market.

s: What is the capital of the Central African Republic, whose President Touadéra won a third term?
x: Bangui is the CAR capital; Conakry is Guinea's.

s: How many countries does the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) integrate into one market?
x: AfCFTA integrates a 54-country African market.

s: Which country hosts both the 2026 NATO summit and COP31?
x: Türkiye hosts the NATO summit at Ankara and COP31 at Antalya; Australia leads the COP31 negotiations.

s: Who is President of Negotiations for COP31 in 2026?
x: COP31 is hosted by Türkiye at Antalya, with Australia as President of Negotiations.

s: Where was the seventh session of the UN Environment Assembly (UNEA-7) held in December 2025?
x: UNEA-7 met at UNEP headquarters in Nairobi on 8-12 December 2025.

s: What was the theme of UNEA-7, held in Nairobi in December 2025?
o: Advancing sustainable solutions for a resilient planet
x: UNEA-7 (8-12 December 2025) had the theme 'Advancing sustainable solutions for a resilient planet'.
